To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there are various barriers to the use and implementation of appropriate infant and child-feeding practices in rural areas of a Ugandan district.

in the rural area of Uganda, the primary caregivers' knowledge, culture, social status, and patterns and the burden of their other responsibilities in the households were the main barriers to appropriate infant and young-child feeding practices.

the main barriers that prevent primary caregivers from using appropriate infant and young-child-feeding practices include: 1) lack of knowledge about appropriate feeding practices, 2) cultural beliefs, 3) influence of other family members, 4) influence of community leaders, 5) influence of health workers, 6) influence of the media, 7) influence of friends, 8) influence of religious leaders, 9) influence of other children's caregivers, 10) lack of time
In summary, our research is concerned with
the barriers that primary caregivers face when they are trying to feed their infants and young children appropriately.
the need for more effective interventions that address these barriers in rural areas of the country.
the identification of barriers to infant and child-feeding practices among the primary caregivers of children under two years of age in rural areas of Iganga District in eastern Uganda.

the main barriers of infant and young child feeding practices in rural Uganda are the lack of knowledge, culture, social status and burden of responsibilities of the primary caregivers.
the primary caregiver's knowledge and culture are the major barriers to the use and implementation of appropriate infant and child-feeding practices in rural Uganda.
the barriers to the practice of appropriate infant and child-feeding are related to the knowledge, culture, social status and burden of other household responsibilities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need to improve the knowledge of primary caregivers on appropriate infant and young-child feeding practices.
the primary caregivers' knowledge and cultural practices are the main factors that hinder the implementation of appropriate infant and child-feeding practices.
the main barriers for the use of appropriate feeding practices are the lack of knowledge, cultural beliefs, and other responsibilities of the primary caregivers.
